scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! Our department is OFF THE NETWORK -- every
single one of our machines, all at once, can't reach anything!! Something
around the box all our wires go into must be wrong, but I don't know what.
Could someone look at it and get us back on the network -- the whole
department is sitting here doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified end-to-end IP connectivity across all departments and the suspected access switches. Multiple cross‑LAN pings are successful with 0% loss and normal RTTs: for example, cs_lab1 (192.168.2.3) to Internet host pc2 (128.168.0.2) works; cs_lab3 to office_pc (192.168.3.2) works; cs_hod to office_pc works; it_lab1/it_lab2 to office_pc/pc2 work; and laptop0 (principle LAN) to pc2 works. The core reachability matrix also shows office_pc, pc0 (principle), pc1 (servers), and pc2–pc5 (Internet LAN) all mutually reachable without loss.

On the suspected “box all our wires go into” devices (access switches), the bridge and member interfaces are up and forwarding: switch1 (CS) shows br0 UP with eth0 and eth1 UP; the same health is seen on switch0 (IT), switch2 (Office), switch3 (Principle), switch4 (Servers), and switch5 (Internet). If an access switch or its uplink were down, local hosts would fail to reach gateways and remote VLANs—contradicted by the successful cross‑department tests above.

Localization: No faults detected on access switches or routers; default gateways are reachable from representative hosts in each LAN.

Root cause: No active network fault found; likely a transient or non-network/local issue outside the lab (e.g., power to a desk switch, cabling, or host-side problem).

Corrective fix: None required on the network. If users still report issues, have local support check power/cables to the desk hub/patch panel and verify host NIC/link status and IP settings.

The agent's conclusion that the IT access switch is not faulty is supported by multiple 0%‑loss ping tests between representative hosts across VLANs and by switch interface checks; most key claims are grounded in the log and the inference (working pings → functioning switch) is logical.
